Nutrition Guide 2026

Panda Express Nutrition: Calories, Macros & the Smartest Way to Order in 2026

Reviewed October 2026 by the Panda Coupons Editorial Team • Panda Express nutrition varies more than almost any fast-food menu, because meals are built à la carte instead of sold as fixed combos. A Bowl alone can run anywhere from 280 to 1,130 calories depending on what you pick, and a Plate stretches from 430 to 1,640. The numbers below come straight from official Panda Express nutrition disclosures.

280–1,130 Bowl Range (kcal)
430–1,640 Plate Range (kcal)
580–2,150+ Bigger Plate (kcal)

Nutrition Details

How We Verify This Data

Every figure in this guide is sourced directly from Panda Express's official Nutrition & Allergen page and cross-checked against our own calculator database. Panda Express states that its values are based on standard recipes, so actual numbers can shift slightly by location, portion size, and prep method. If you're managing a medical condition or a severe allergy, confirm details in-app or in-store before ordering — this guide is a planning tool, not a substitute for that.

Panda Express Meal Sizes at a Glance

The range is this wide because Panda Express doesn't set fixed combos — every entrée and side is priced and calculated individually, so your total depends entirely on what goes into the bowl. A White Rice and Grilled Teriyaki Chicken bowl and a Fried Rice and Orange Chicken bowl are both technically "a Bowl," but they're 800+ calories apart.

Panda Express Meal Formats and Calorie Ranges Comparison
Meal FormatItems IncludedCaloric RangeKey Takeaway
Bowl1 Side + 1 Entrée280–1,130 kcalIdeal for single portions; wide calorie swing based on side chosen
Plate1 Side + 2 Entrées430–1,640 kcalStandard dinner; best protein yield per dollar when choosing lean meats
Bigger Plate1 Side + 3 Entrées580–2,150+ kcalRoughly 580–2,150+ calories, based on combining official per-item figures
Panda BundleAny Size Meal + Medium Drink280–2,560 kcalSugary drinks can add 200–400+ calories; opt for water or zero-calorie soda

Panda Express Calories by Category

Detailed breakdown of all official menu departments. Review exact calories, sodium, and macronutrient trends before customizing your plate:

Sides

130–620 cal
  • Super Greens 130 cal
  • White Steamed Rice 520 cal | 0mg sod
  • Chow Mein 600 cal | 1000mg sod
  • Fried Rice 620 cal | 1000mg sod

Sides swing harder than any other category. Super Greens sits at 130 calories, while Fried Rice reaches 620. The difference isn't really the rice or the greens — it's the oil, egg, and seasoning used in wok preparation. White Steamed Rice lands at 520 calories with zero sodium, making it the cleanest carb option if sodium is your concern.

Chicken Entrées

210–490 cal
  • Grilled Teriyaki Chicken 300 cal | 36g P
  • Black Pepper Chicken 280 cal | 1060mg sod
  • Kung Pao Chicken 290 cal | 930mg sod
  • The Original Orange Chicken 490 cal | 25g P

Grilled Teriyaki Chicken is the standout here: 300 calories and 36 grams of protein, the highest protein count on the wok menu. Orange Chicken, the chain's best-known dish, runs 490 calories with 25 grams of protein and 30 grams of sugar — batter and glaze account for most of that gap. Kung Pao Chicken (290 cal, 930mg sodium) and Black Pepper Chicken (280 cal, 1060mg sodium) offer moderate calories with savory seasonings.

Chicken Breast

210–380 cal
  • String Bean Chicken Breast 210 cal | 17g P
  • Honey Sesame Chicken Breast 420 cal | Sweet Glaze
  • SweetFire Chicken Breast 380 cal | Crisp Glaze

This line trades a little batter for leaner numbers. String Bean Chicken Breast comes in at 210 calories with 17 grams of protein and dietary fiber from fresh string beans. SweetFire Chicken Breast (380 cal) and Honey Sesame Chicken Breast (420 cal) lean sweeter with delicious glazes.

Beef

150–470 cal
  • Broccoli Beef 150 cal | 9g P
  • Beijing Beef 470 cal | 24g F

Broccoli Beef is the lightest entrée on the menu at 150 calories with 9 grams of protein — a strong pick for lower-calorie dining. Beijing Beef is battered and crispy, landing at 470 calories with 24 grams of fat.

Seafood

250–430 cal
  • Kung Pao Shrimp 250 cal | 22g P
  • Honey Walnut Shrimp 430 cal | Sweet Glaze

Honey Walnut Shrimp (430 cal) features tempura shrimp tossed in honey sauce with candied walnuts. Kung Pao Shrimp (250 cal, 22g protein) provides a savory, spicy seafood alternative wok-tossed with peanuts and chili peppers.

Vegetables & Tofu

130–340 cal
  • Super Greens (Side Portion) 130 cal | 9g P
  • Eggplant Tofu 340 cal | 8g P

Super Greens (130 cal) delivers a blend of steamed broccoli, kale, and cabbage with 7g of dietary fiber. Eggplant Tofu (340 cal, 8g protein) pairs tofu and eggplant in sweet-spicy ginger garlic sauce.

Appetizers

150–200 cal
  • Chicken Potstickers 190 cal | 10g P
  • Chicken Egg Roll 200 cal | 12g F
  • Veggie Spring Roll 160 cal | 19g C
  • Cream Cheese Rangoon 190 cal | 9g F

Veggie Spring Rolls (160 cal) and Chicken Egg Rolls (200 cal) offer crispy flavor. Cream Cheese Rangoons (190 cal) provide sweet cream cheese in wonton wrappers.

Soup

65–110 cal
  • Egg Drop Soup 65 cal | 900mg sod
  • Hot & Sour Soup 90 cal | 1290mg sod
  • Wonton Soup 110 cal | 800mg sod

Hot & Sour Soup (90 cal) carries 1290mg of sodium. Egg Drop Soup (65 cal) is a lighter option with 4g protein.

Sauces

20–70 cal
  • Chili Sauce 20 cal | 310mg sod
  • Sweet & Sour Sauce 70 cal | 17g sugar
  • Teriyaki Sauce 30 cal | 310mg sod

Sauces add extra flavor. Sweet & Sour Sauce adds 70 calories and 17g sugar per cup, while Teriyaki Sauce adds 30 calories.

Cub Meals (Kids)

Under 600 cal
  • Grilled Teriyaki Cub Meal Balanced Protein
  • Orange Chicken Cub Meal Kid Favorite
  • Broccoli Beef Cub Meal Lean Beef & Veggies

Panda Express designed its Cub Meals around balanced nutrition for children. Each one includes a junior entrée, junior side, and fruit.

Orange Chicken Nutrition — The Deep Dive

A single serving of Orange Chicken (5.7 oz) contains 490 calories, 22 grams of fat, 57 grams of carbohydrate, 30 grams of sugar, and 25 grams of protein, with 820mg of sodium. These figures reflect Panda Express's official nutrition guide disclosure.

Why Orange Chicken Is the Highest-Calorie Chicken Entrée

The chicken is battered and deep-fried first, then coated in a sugar-based glaze. Both steps add calories independently: the batter absorbs oil during frying, and the glaze adds nearly all 30 grams of sugar on top of that. Neither step is unusual for fast food — it's just compounding on a dish that's already fried.

Orange Chicken vs. Grilled Teriyaki Chicken

Nutritional Comparison between Orange Chicken and Grilled Teriyaki Chicken
Nutritional MetricOrange ChickenGrilled Teriyaki ChickenDifference
Calories490 kcal300 kcal-190 kcal (39% fewer calories)
Protein25g36g+11g (+44% more protein)
Sodium820mg530mg-290mg (35% less sodium)
Sugar30g10g-20g (67% less sugar)

Grilled Teriyaki Chicken delivers roughly double the protein-per-calorie ratio compared to Orange Chicken with significantly less sugar and fat.

The #1 Nutritional Swap on the Menu

Swapping a side of Fried Rice (620 cal) for Super Greens (130 cal) in a Bowl saves about 490 calories and 630mg of sodium in one change — the single biggest impact swap available anywhere on the menu.

Is Panda Express Healthy?

The honest answer: it depends entirely on which entrée and side you pick, because the range runs from a 280-calorie Bowl to a 2,150-calorie Bigger Plate. Panda Express isn't inherently unhealthy or healthy — it's an à la carte menu where the choice matters more than the restaurant.

The Wok Smart Line

Wok Smart is Panda Express's designation for entrées that are lower in calories, fat, and sodium relative to the rest of the menu — generally the grilled and steamed options like Grilled Teriyaki Chicken, Broccoli Beef, and Super Greens. It exists specifically to make healthier scanning easier without needing a calculator.

Kids LiveWell / Cub Meal Criteria

Panda Express's Cub Meals are built to meet Kids LiveWell program criteria, verified by the National Restaurant Association against nutrition guidelines from major health organizations. Each Cub Meal stays under 600 calories and includes a vegetable and a fruit serving by design, not as an afterthought.

Building a Lower-Calorie, Lower-Sodium, or Higher-Protein Plate

For Fewer Calories

Choose Super Greens (130 cal) instead of starch sides like Fried Rice (620 cal) or Chow Mein (600 cal) to cut nearly 500 calories per meal. Pick a Bowl over a Plate, and ask for sauce on the side.

For More Protein

Grilled Teriyaki Chicken (36g protein, 300 cal) is the highest-protein entrée on the menu.

For Less Sodium

Watch high-sodium specialty items specifically. Grilled Teriyaki Chicken (530mg) and Broccoli Beef (660mg) are among the lower-sodium entrée options.

Allergens & Ingredients: What's Actually Safe

Panda Express states it uses ingredients containing all major FDA allergens — wheat, soy, egg, milk, tree nuts, peanuts, shellfish, fish, and sesame — and that cross-contact is possible in any item because food is prepared on shared equipment. No menu item can be guaranteed allergen-free.

What's Gluten-Free at Panda Express

White Steamed Rice and Super Greens are the safest base choices, since neither lists wheat on the official allergen sheet. Broccoli Beef also skips the wheat flag, though it still lists soy. Orange Chicken, Chow Mein, and most sauce-based dishes all contain wheat, mainly from soy sauce and batter.

The Peanut Oil Question, Answered Directly

Panda Express does not cook with peanut oil — it uses soybean oil for frying and stir-frying. That said, several dishes (Kung Pao Chicken specifically) do contain actual peanuts as an ingredient, so "no peanut oil" doesn't mean "peanut-free." Check the allergen flag on the specific dish, not just the cooking oil.

Official Verification

For anything allergy-critical, don't rely solely on this guide or any third-party page — Panda Express provides a dedicated allergen lookup and a customer service line at (800) 877-8988 for direct confirmation before you order.

What This Guide Can't Tell You

Panda Express prepares food fresh in small batches, so actual nutrition can vary by location, portion scooping, and regional recipe differences. These figures reflect standard recipes as published by Panda Express, not a lab measurement of your specific order. If you have celiac disease or a severe allergy, treat every number here as a starting point, not a guarantee, and confirm with the restaurant directly.

Panda Express Nutrition FAQs

How many calories are in Panda Express Orange Chicken? ▾
A standard serving of Orange Chicken has 490 calories, 22 grams of fat, and 30 grams of sugar, according to Panda Express's official nutrition data.
Is Panda Express healthy? ▾
It depends on your order rather than the restaurant itself — meals range from 280 to over 2,000 calories depending on entrée and side choices, so the same visit can be a light meal or a heavy one based entirely on what you pick.
What is the healthiest thing to order at Panda Express? ▾
Grilled Teriyaki Chicken (300 cal) paired with Super Greens (130 cal) is one of the strongest combinations on the menu: 36g protein and low saturated fat.
Does Panda Express use peanut oil? ▾
No. Panda Express cooks with soybean oil, not peanut oil. However, some dishes like Kung Pao Chicken do contain actual peanuts as an ingredient, so check the specific dish's allergen flag rather than assuming the oil alone makes it peanut-safe.
What's gluten-free at Panda Express? ▾
White Steamed Rice and Super Greens are the two menu items that don't list wheat as an allergen. Most sauce-based entrées, including Orange Chicken and Chow Mein, contain wheat through soy sauce or batter.
How many calories are in a Panda Express Bowl vs. Plate vs. Bigger Plate? ▾
A Bowl (one side, one entrée) ranges from 280 to 1,130 calories. A Plate (one side, two entrées) ranges from 430 to 1,640 calories. A Bigger Plate (one side, three entrées) typically runs from about 580 to 2,150 or more calories, based on combining official per-item figures.
What can't this nutrition guide tell you? ▾
It can't account for portion variation by location, seasonal menu changes, or how a specific store prepares your order. These are standard recipe values published by Panda Express, not a measurement of your exact meal.
Where can I verify this data officially? ▾
Panda Express publishes its full nutrition and allergen sheet directly on its website, and you can also call (800) 877-8988 for direct confirmation on any item.
